'''Ethel Moustacchi''' (21 August 1933 - 13 December 2016)<ref name=":0">Mathilde Regnault, Disparition d'Ethel Moustacchi [https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcurie.fr%2Factualite%2Farchive%2Fdisparition-dethel-moustacchi#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url archive], Institut Curie press release, 16 December 2016.</ref> was an Egyptian-born French geneticist and research director of the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS). She was a leading figure in [[molecular biology]] and [[radiobiology]] research.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Prix d'Honneur Inserm 2011 ETHEL MOUSTACCHI |url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=http://www.inserm.fr/content/download/49565/317709/file/portrait_ethel_moustaki.pdf/index.html#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=archive.wikiwix.com}}</ref> From 1988, she headed the  Société française de génétique (French Genetic Society).<ref name=np/> She is remembered in particular for her interest in the mechanisms of [[mutagenesis]] and [[DNA repair]], for her research into [[Fanconi anemia]] and for her call for more attention to be given to the health effects of small doses of radiation on nuclear workers and healthcare professionals.<ref name=":0"/>

In early 2026, Moustacchi was confirmed to be one of the 72 women to have their names added to those of [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|the men already engraved on the Eiffel Tower]].

== Early life and education ==
Esther Ethel Moustacchi was born in [[Cairo]], Egypt, on 21 August 1933. Her father, Felix P. Moustacchi, was a Greek from [[Corfu]], while her mother Flora (née Revi) was born in Cairo but came from a family established in [[Trieste]]. Ethel was their first child.<ref name=np>{{cite web|url=https://musee.curie.fr/blog/ethel-moustacchi-1933-2016|title=Ethel Moustacchi [1933-2016]|author=Pigeard, Natalie|publisher=Musée Curie|date=5 April 2026|access-date=4 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=http://archive.org/details/whoswhoinscience0000unse_p3k9 |title=Who's who in science and engineering : 2002-2003, millennium edition |date=2001 |publisher=New Providence, NJ : Marquis Who's Who |others=Internet Archive |isbn=978-0-8379-5760-9}}</ref><ref name=":3">[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 2026-02-13</ref> After first attending an Italian-speaking primary school, she became a student at the French lycée in Cairo where she passed her [[baccalauréat]].<ref name=np/> When only 17, on her own insistence, she moved to France in September 1951 to embark on her higher education, initially studying in [[Montpellier]] and then at the [[:fr:Faculté des sciences de Paris|faculté des sciences de Paris]] where she studied chemistry and biology.<ref name=":0"/><ref name=np/>

Moustacchi first spent a preparatory year in sciences at the [[University of Montpellier]],<ref name=np/>  then enrolled at the [[Chimie ParisTech|École Nationale Supérieure de Chimie de Paris]], and in 1954 joined the Institut du Radium, later the [[Curie Institute (Paris)|Curie Institute in Paris]], where she subsequently spent most of her career.<ref name=":0"/> She initially studied under geneticist [[Boris Ephrussi]]. Recruited by the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) in 1959, she began a thesis on the factors of radioresistance in yeast ({{Langx|fr|Facteurs de la sensibilité des levures à l'action létale des radiations ionisantes : étude d'un mutant radio-résistant}})<ref name=np/> under the supervision of {{ill|Raymond Latarjet|fr}}, which she defended in 1964.<ref name=":0"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=CEA |date=2026-02-20 |title=Quatre femmes scientifiques du CEA bientôt inscrites sur la Tour Eiffel |url=https://www.cea.fr/drf/Pages/Actualites/Vie-de-la-DRF/2026/quatre-femmes-scientifiques-du-CEA-bientot-inscrites-sur-la-tour-Eiffel.aspx |access-date=2026-04-17 |website=CEA/Fabrique de savoirs |language=fr}}</ref>

== Career ==
Moustacchi left France to pursue postdoctoral studies in the United States and collaborated with Donald Williamson in [[Herschel L. Roman]]'s laboratory at [[Washington State University]] in [[Seattle]].<ref name=":4" />

In 1966, aged 33 she returned to France and took over as head of the radio-biology laboratory at the [[Paris-Sud University|faculté des sciences d'Orsay]], a satellite branch of l'Institut du radium, and focused her research towards study of DNA damage.<ref name=":4" />

In 1985, she returned to the Curie Institute's Paris site, taking over Raymond Latarjet's laboratory and focusing on the mechanisms of [[mutagenesis]] and DNA repair through a [[pathophysiology]] approach to [[chemotherapy]] and [[Radiation therapy|radiotherapy]] induced cancers. She also worked for over a decade on [[Fanconi anemia|Fanconi's anemia]], a rare genetic disease affecting the bone marrow.<ref name=":0"/>

From 1988 to 1992, she headed to French Genetic Institute<ref name=np/> and from 1995, became a scientific advisor for the [[Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives]] (CEA), she called for more attention to be given to the health effects of small doses of radiation on nuclear workers and healthcare professionals.<ref name=":0"/>

Moustacchi headed the joint CNRS/Curie Institute UMR218 unit until her retirement in 1998.<ref name=":4" />

In 1995, she became scientific advise for biology at the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission]].<ref name=":0"/>

Her successor at the French Genetic Institute, [[Geneviève Almouzni]], complemented her on the encouragement and inspiration she and her team received from Ethel Moustacchi. She was "always attentive to the younger members of the unit and was constantly available for advice."<ref name=np/>

Moustacchi died in the [[14th arrondissement of Paris]] on 13 December 2016, aged 83.<ref>{{Cite web |title=matchID - Moteur de recherche des décès |url=https://deces.matchid.io/id/t_9lp-8Qp0Ba |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=deces.matchid.io}}</ref>

== Awards and commemoration ==
Moustacchi was appointed [[Legion of Honour|Chevalier de la Légion d'Honneur]] in 1999 and promoted to ''Officier'' in 2013.<ref name=":0"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Décret du 31 décembre 1999 portant promotion et nomination - Légifrance |url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000000580150 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250315203244/https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000000580150 |archive-date=2025-03-15 |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=www.legifrance.gouv.fr |language=fr |url-status=live }}</ref>

In [[2011 in science|2011]], Ethel Moustacchi received the Prix d'honneur de l'[[Inserm]] for her life's work.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7-qN8xymg4E |title=Ethel Moustacchi, Prix d'Honneur Inserm 2011 |date=2013-10-10 |last=LaChaine CASDEN |access-date=2026-02-13 |via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Les Prix Inserm · Inserm, La science pour la santé |url=https://www.inserm.fr/nous-connaitre/prix-inserm/ |access-date=2026-02-14 |website=Inserm |language=fr-FR}}</ref> She was also the recipient of the Pierre and Marie Curie Medal from the International Society for Radiobiology in French.<ref name=":0"/>

In 2026, Moustacchi was announced as one of 72 historical women in STEM whose names have been proposed to be added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|72 men]] already celebrated on the [[Eiffel Tower]]. The plan was announced by the Mayor of Paris, [[Anne Hidalgo]] following the recommendations of a committee led by [[Isabelle Vauglin]] of ''[[Femmes et Sciences]]'' and Jean-François Martins, representing the operating company which runs the Eiffel Tower.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eiffel Tower: a list of 72 women scientists will soon be inscribed on the Parisian monument |url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/en/news/in-paris/articles/340564-eiffel-tower-list-of-72-women-scientists-soon-to-be-honored-on-the-paris-landmark |access-date=2026-02-14 |website=www.sortiraparis.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-26 |title=Eiffel Tower to honor 72 women scientists for posterity |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/01/26/eiffel-tower-to-honor-72-women-in-science-for-posterity_6749828_7.html |access-date=2026-02-14 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Les noms des 72 femmes pour la Tour Eiffel ont été révélés. |url=https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/news/les-noms-des-72-femmes-pour-la-tour-eiffel-ont-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-r%C3%A9v%C3%A9l%C3%A9 |access-date=2026-02-14 |website=Femmes & Sciences |language=fr}}</ref><ref name=":3" />
